T: Old trees. In the garden, they were hedges once.
M: The hillside, honeycombed with old mine workings.
E: The mine. The beams are newer than you'd think. Somebody's been working down there.
Z: A statue of a woman in a gardener's apron, her face worn smooth, as if someone wanted it forgotten.
f: An old flowerbed, all weeds now.
w: A dry fountain, full of leaves.
^: North: back up to Warrior City.

lines: Planted by the old king, who loved quiet things more than loud ones.
The king trained his army hard, but only so his people would be safe.
His advisors began to whisper that his heart had turned to war. Some say a shadow had crept into theirs.
The whispers spread. The king was mad, they said. He dreamed of battles in his sleep.
His own people began to fear him.
One morning, walking here alone, the king met a woman tending the roses.
There was something about her. His friends warned him that she wanted more than roses.
But his people had turned from him, and his friends doubted him, and she knew exactly what to say to his doubts.
They were married here, under the old arch. They had a son.
Five years on, the royal army was the strongest force in all the land. The king listened to no one but his queen.
And the queen said: strike first. And so the kingdom readied itself for war.
The rest of the stone has broken away.

objects.name: Old Gardener
lines: Nobody tends this garden any more. I come and pull a weed now and then. For the old king.
He was kind, whatever they say.

answer: Nobody knows her name. It was taken off everything after.
She just... wasn't, one day. And the king was gone too, not long after.
The prince? Lost, they wrote. Not dead. Lost.
I'd like to think he's out there somewhere, sleeping it off.

questions.ask: Pulling weeds for a gone king? Sad.
